claims.title: Diverse-sample agreement: doomed precision + anti-circularity
claims.paper: floor+siginject 98% in-family precision (fires 65, 1 false-abandon, 100% recall); Agentless recovers 0 on the doomed set (anti-circularity); 75.4% independent
claims.reproduced:
configs: ['floor', 'implicit20', 'implicit40', 'p8c', 'phaseStaged_b35', 'planFirst_b20', 'siginject_b10x3', 'signaled10', 'toolAlloc_b20', 'twopass_b10p15']
n=150; oracle-union 86/150; DOOMED(0/10) 64/150

ABANDON signal (all budget-configs fail -> predict doomed):
  [floor                 ] fires  75  false-abandon 11  precision  85%  recall 100%
  [floor+siginject       ] fires  65  false-abandon  1  precision  98%  recall 100%
  [floor+siginject+planFirst] fires  65  false-abandon  1  precision  98%  recall 100%

COST-RESOLUTION frontier on n=150 ($ = modeled cost_usd):
  policy                                 resolve    cost$   turns
  floor (b10)                            75/150   $ 69.94    3012
  siginject (b10x3)                      62/150   $ 48.80    2289
  implicit40 (b40)                       69/150   $ 61.37    2752
  2-config select: floor+siginject       85/150   $118.75    5301
  3-config escalate: +planFirst          85/150   $161.86    7825

ABANDON TRADE (2-config select, then abandon-if-both-fail vs add a 3rd escalation tier):
  both-fail instances: 65  (abandon them)
  a 3rd tier (planFirst) would recover 0 of them at +$19.58
  -> abandon SAVES $19.58 to lose 0 resolve(s): the cross-sample doomed signal is the cost lever the repro never delivered.

=== CROSS-MODEL within-tier replication (best 2-config abandon pair) ===
  Sonnet  n=150 doomed= 64: best pair [floor+siginject_b10x3] precision 98% (fires 65, false-abandon 1)
  Haiku   n=150 doomed= 76: best pair [floor+implicit40] precision 97% (fires 78, false-abandon 2)
  -> mechanism replicates across tiers; partner config is model-specific.

=== OPUS-TIER abandon-vs-escalate boundary (n=65 Sonnet-doomed) ===
  Opus floor 15 | Opus siginject 12 | union 16 (diverse: +1/4 each unique)
  escalate-tier reach 16/65 (25%) at modeled $120.23 = $7.51/resolve (vs $1.40 base => marginal; confirms Phase 8/9 negative)
  both-Opus-fail 49; Agentless recovers 0 => ABANDON precision 100% (doomed across 5 configs / 2 tiers / 2 harnesses)
  -> ABANDON is the economical default; the agreement mechanism FIRES at the Opus tier.

=== LOW->HIGH ladder: Haiku agreement-fail (floor+implicit40) -> Sonnet/Opus (n=150) ===
  Haiku agreement-fail (doomed): 78/150
  escalate -> Sonnet recovers 10 (13%); Opus recovers 26 (33%); either 26
  truly-doomed up to Opus: 52/150 (abandon-safe across 3 tiers)
  Sonnet-escalation cost $47.45 -> $4.74/resolve (marginal, > $1.40 base).
  -> low->high recovers MORE than mid->high (weaker start = more headroom) but stays a costly tail.

claims.title: Value-of-resolve decision rule (escalation economics)
claims.paper: base $1.40/resolve; tier escalation $2.20 / $3.07 / $7.51 per recovered resolve
claims.reproduced:
BASE (2-config diverse-select): 85/150 resolved at $118.75 => $1.40 per resolve  (always worth it for value-of-resolve V > $1.40)

escalation option                        recovers   $ total  $/resolve  escalate iff V >=
  Sonnet-doomed -> Opus (1 config)  15/65  (23%)   $ 46.12   $   3.07   $3.07
  Sonnet-doomed -> Opus (2 configs)  16/65  (25%)   $120.23   $   7.51   $7.51
  Haiku-doomed -> Opus (1 config)   26/78  (33%)   $ 57.23   $   2.20   $2.20

DECISION RULE: run the base everywhere (V > $1.40); escalate the agreement-doomed set to a stronger tier ONLY when value-of-resolve V exceeds that option's $/resolve ($2.20 cheapest to $7.51 richest). The 3-tier+harness core never recovers: abandon at any V.
